correctness.rationale: Signed Cauchy–Binet proves the weighted matrix-tree identity over integers. The mod-two Fibonacci recurrence gives the global parity obstruction. Exact six-periodic continuants provide a zero precisely at 3|n and a ±1 coefficient otherwise. A single spoke sign flip yields a coefficient of ±2 at resonance, and an explicit null vector with k zero entries plus a global sign reversal yields 2^{k+1} distinct zero frequencies. Direct independent enumeration and exact Walsh transforms agree with determinant values for n=1..9 at every frequency, with longer witness checks to n=150; these finite tests support but do not replace the all-n proof.

originality.rationale: Chebotarev proves the classical unsigned Fibonacci count for rooted path forests/fan trees, and Bogdanowicz proves its Laplacian determinant formula. Weighted matrix-tree theory reduces arbitrary signs to a determinant. These premises do not by themselves state or prove a sharp full Boolean Walsh zero classification, a least nonzero multiplier of exactly one/two, or an exponential family of vanishing signed frequencies. Dedicated searches of the published mathematical result index and relevant primary texts located no statement dominating this combined theorem. This is a bounded best-knowledge novelty assessment, not an independence or priority certificate.
residual_risks: An earlier equivalent result formulated as a singular signed continuant or arbitrary-sign fan Kirchhoff cofactor could exist outside the checked literature.
Published mathematical index results are semantic search hits, not an exhaustive full-text corpus; full text of two nearest indexed findings could not be fetched.
The contribution is a structural spectral classification built from classical ingredients, not a general theorem about all graph families.
